questionText: What is the Spring Initializr and how do you use it?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can define Spring Initializr, choose a Java 17 and Spring Boot 3.3.1 project, explain the generated assets, and verify the project before adding business code.
inScope: Import, inspect, test, and run workflow
outOfScope: A claim that Initializr runs inside the generated application
A claim that it designs the production architecture

claims.statement: Spring Initializr provides an extensible API for generating JVM-based projects and for exposing the metadata used to generate them.
An Initializr project description can include build system, language, packaging, coordinates, platform version, Java version, configuration format, and requested dependencies.
Initializr services can be used by web, command-line, and IDE clients that read service metadata and request generated assets.
This repository's example deliberately selects Spring Boot 3.3.1 and Java 17 as its learning baseline rather than claiming they are current Initializr defaults.
Generated project assets provide a starting structure; application architecture, security, domain rules, deployment, and production verification remain the team's responsibility.

validation.command: Review Java 17 syntax and Spring Boot application entry point against the generated-project explanation
validation.expected: The focused main class is valid with the generated Spring Boot build and is clearly labelled as a starting point

visuals.title: Project choices, generated assets, verification, and first feature

notes: The official Initializr source is used only for project-generation behavior; Boot runtime claims remain tied to the pinned Boot source.

review.notes: Generation metadata, supported client types, and generator boundaries were checked against the official Initializr guide. The 3.3.1 and Java 17 selection is clearly a repository baseline, not a current-service-default claim.
